value: lowest threshold observed at 200 Hz, 86.4 ± 3.4 dB
units: dB re 1 mPa as printed in the abstract (re 1 µPa is the usual underwater reference; the paper writes mPa throughout, probably a misprint)
method: auditory evoked potential (AEP) audiometry with tone bursts; threshold is the lowest sound pressure level giving a repeatable AEP trace
conditions: juvenile fish, standard length 6.99 ± 0.51 cm, wet mass 19.47 ± 2.93 g, from a commercial company (Dalian Tianzheng Industrial Co., Ltd.; farm or wild origin not stated); 80 fish held, AEP run on 8, one died, waveforms from 7; anaesthetised with MS-222 (1:14000) and immobilised with gallamine triiodide (1.2-1.4 mg/g) for recording; rearing water 21.4-22.8 C; only four tone-burst frequencies tested (100, 200, 300, 500 Hz, chosen from offshore wind turbine noise), so this is the lowest of four points and not a full audiogram; thresholds tended to rise from 200 up to 500 Hz; hydrophone sensitivity -190 dB re 1 mPa as printed

method: exudate assay: mucus-like fluid released in one minute of exposure to air mixed with CO2, compared across 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100% CO2
conditions: adult worms (visible clitellum) kept in lab bins, source not stated, mass not reported; 0% CO2 is room air; exposure one minute through a nozzle in a covered dish; dose-dependent rise across the series (n = 12-20 per the Results, p < 0.0001); the text gives no pairwise test of 0% against 100%, and its ANOVA is called one-way in the Methods and figure caption but two-way in the Results; worms rinsed with distilled water before the assay released significantly more exudate (n = 6-12); 25% CO2 gave no significant response

source.title: Mechanisms of carbon dioxide detection in the earthworm Dendrobaena veneta

quote: Earthworms excreted the most exudate in response to 100% CO2.
note: Licence CC BY (line on the PDF; Crossref lists CC BY 4.0). Read on the Frontiers PDF through WebFetch. The paper names the species Dendrobaena veneta and says it was previously known as Eisenia hortensis. GBIF holds both as separate species: Dendrobaena veneta (Rosa, 1886), gbif.org/species/5739805, and Dendrobaena hortensis (Michaelsen, 1890), gbif.org/species/7725323, whose synonyms include Eisenia hortensis and Dendrobaena veneta hortensis but not D. veneta. The paper's two names therefore point at different GBIF species and the worms' identity is uncertain; filed under the binomial the paper prints. Neither name is in gbif-names.tsv; owner to confirm. Exudate release is the authors' proxy for aversion, not a direct sensory recording.

value: the CO2-evoked exudate response was significantly reduced by acetazolamide, a carbonic anhydrase inhibitor (p < 0.01, n = 8-13)
method: exudate assay with pharmacological blockers applied before CO2 exposure
conditions: adult worms (visible clitellum), source not stated; soaked 10 minutes in 5 ml of 50 mM acetazolamide (vehicle water) in a 10 ml tube, blotted dry, then tested in the one-minute exudate assay at 0, 50 and 100% CO2 (exudate release is the authors' aversion proxy); acetazolamide did not reduce the response to the AITC positive control; amiloride, diminazene aceturate, ruthenium red and indisulam also reduced the CO2 response (diminazene and 5 mM amiloride also reduced the AITC response)
